handback.t:
R4-A2 / H2 report. Result: NEGATIVE. No RRF, RSF or top-20 rerank variant raises end-to-end routing success over spell-correct dense. Everything is synthetic-until-validated-on-real-traffic. Nothing was applied to src/.

**What I built (all under my h2 prefix)**
- Bins: `src/bin/h2_route.rs` (end-to-end), `src/bin/h2_retrieval.rs` (doc-level), engine `src/bin/h2_common/mod.rs`.
- Python and fixtures: `py/h2_embed.py`, `py/h2_summary.py`, `results/h2_*`.
- Variants judged: dense+spell, tf-idf hybrid with tuned alpha, RRF (k=60), RSF, and top-20 rerank with three cheap scorers (IDF token overlap, BM25-style coverage, 8-feature logistic).
- The h2 engine is a copy of g16's worlds and policy engine, so it replays g16's `R0` and `G-post+g1` bit-exactly (worst |d| 5.55e-17 over 8 worlds).
- One new control, `ctl-noinfo`: task text is always drawn from a random other concept while the best agent still depends on the true concept.
- The logistic is trained offline on corpus C with ground-truth same-concept labels, so its gains are optimistic.
- Fresh corpora C2 and D2 come from `g1_corpus.py` seeds 5 and 6, embedded with MiniLM only. They re-instantiate the same 240 concept templates, so this is a text replication, not new domains.
- Protocol: tune on seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60 on corpus A, frozen confirms on B, C2, D2 at seeds 61-90, paired CI with Holm, TOST in the json. A repeat of the B confirm was byte-identical.

**Findings**
- **Spell-correct was already the main lever.** Under the g1 gate, spell-dense beats raw dense by +.034 in sib16 and +.017 in drift on A, and similarly on all three confirms.
- **The g1 gate fails every control.** Every variant, including g16's `R0`, has Holm losses in ctl-irrel and ctl-oneoff on A and on all three confirms (-.014 to -.028). The g1 gate stays opt-in only.
- **The literal keep rule does not discriminate.** Vs the same front (guarded) with no retrieval: at least 2 treatment-world Holm wins and no Holm loss in ctl-irrel, ctl-oneoff, ctl-noinfo, on A plus 2 of 3 confirms. Only variants under g16's safe gate pass:
  - the passing set is safe-gate dense, hybrid, RSF, rerank-logit, and even raw dense with no spell-correct;
  - so the gate drives the pass, not the retrieval.
- **No variant adds over spell-only.** Added after seeing pass 1: the variant must beat spell-only under the same gate (Holm win in ≥2 treatment worlds, no Holm loss in any world). 0 of 14 pass.
  - g1-gate hybrid and bm25-rerank gain +.019 to +.025 in sib16 on all four corpora, but lose -.025 to -.031 in rand16.
  - Safe-gate variants have no Holm win over spell-only anywhere.
- **Retrieval gains do not transfer.** Doc-level F1@3 / MRR / hit@1 on A:

| System | F1@3 | MRR | hit@1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| dense+spell | .626 | .946 | .915 |
| hybrid (z-fusion, alpha .8) | .552 | .961 | .943 |
| RRF | .457 | .940 | .905 |
| RSF | .557 | .960 | .940 |
| rerank-logit | .654 | .960 | .940 |

  - Only the logistic reranker raises F1@3 (+.028), yet it is -.001 in sib16 end-to-end under the safe gate.
  - RRF is worse than plain dense on both F1@3 and MRR.
- **Cost.** In the routing loop, spell-dense or hybrid cost 5.5-8.3 µs/task; RRF and RSF cost 33-36 µs/task, about 5x, for no gain.
  - Rerank-20 averages 12.3 scorer calls per task. Measured scorer cost is 0.13-0.21 µs per call; I charge a configurable, deliberately pessimistic 2 µs per call.
  - On the doc-level 780-doc benchmark the first-stage dense scan is 223 µs. RRF fusion adds 7.8 µs and RSF 5.3 µs.
- **The safe gate is not strictly harmless.** There are small Holm control losses of -.004 to -.007 in ctl-irrel (C2, D2) and ctl-oneoff (A, B, C2) for a few variants.

**Caveats you should know**
- RRF and RSF need an absolute admission floor; I put it on the dense cosine, so they collapse onto the dense arm. Other floors were not tried.
- Post-hoc changes, disclosed in the entry: the raw-dense arm was added after pass 1 (pass-1 files kept as `h2_route_pass1.*`), the strict "adds over spell" rule, and the ±.01 non-inferiority margin (copied from g16). The literal pre-declared rule is reported unchanged.
- Corpus A is the tuning and held-out corpus; B, C2, D2 are frozen confirms.
- Oracle similarity gains +.166 / +.167 / +.088 / +.105 (sib16 / rand16 / sib64 / drift) over the same front. The best real similarity gets about 25-65% of that, so retrieval quality is still the headroom.

**Proposal** (in `results/h2_proposed_patch.md`)
- Adopt none of RRF, RSF or rerank-20.
- If g16's safe gate is adopted opt-in, spell-corrected MiniLM alone ties the tf-idf hybrid under that gate (|d| ≤ .011, all n.s.), so the sparse leg could be dropped.
